correctness.rationale: At level \(\ell\), all old vertices of \(HK_{\ell-1}\) form one bipartition class and the newly inserted midpoints form the other, while the lifted symmetric Krawtchouk Hamiltonian has zero diagonal. The source entry formula shows that each nonzero off-diagonal weight is a positive layer factor divided by the appropriate forward/backward degree. The two new midpoints replacing a fixed old edge therefore give duplicate columns, and after keeping one from each pair the old-to-new block is diagonally equivalent to the unsigned vertex-edge incidence matrix of \(HK_{\ell-1}\). Because \(HK_{\ell-1}\) is connected and bipartite, that incidence matrix has rank \(|V(HK_{\ell-1})|-1\). Hence the block-off-diagonal Hamiltonian has rank twice this number. Substituting \(|V(HK_j)|=(2\cdot4^j+4)/3\) gives \(\dim\ker H_\ell=(4^\ell+2)/3=|V(HK_\ell)|/2\). Independent exact incidence-rank computations for levels one through six reproduced nullities \(2,6,22,86,342,1366\). The finite calculations only corroborate the arbitrary-level incidence proof. Chiral sign conjugation across the two bipartition classes pairs every nonzero eigenvalue with its negative, so exactly one quarter of the normalized spectrum lies below zero and three quarters at or below zero.
risks: The result uses the zero-diagonal symmetric Krawtchouk lift specified in the record; adding diagonal magnetic fields destroys the chiral argument.
